scope: Independent review of the live launcher, guest/host worker, public fixtures, transfer campaign, relay orchestration and recording scripts. No production edits or redundant builds were performed.
exclusions: crates/spiralcore-mvm-adapter/src/live.rs and related adapter changes authored by this reviewer
crates/spiralcore-mvm-live/mvm-patch packaging authored by this reviewer
upstream MVM implementation reviewed by another agent
full pilot arithmetic is recorded separately in qualification/measurement-review.json

findings.description: The receiver process CPU timer starts after framed receive, excluding socket reads, frame allocation and copy. Summing it with sender CPU must not be labeled complete endpoint CPU.
findings.resolution: Derived rows now use sender_reported_cpu_us, receiver_processing_cpu_us and sender_plus_receiver_processing_cpu_us, with an explicit CPU-scope statement that excludes framed receive and distinguishes guest and host accounting domains. Raw historical receipts are unchanged.
findings.delivery_requirement: Report host OS lifecycle CPU separately, avoid double-counting nested guest/worker CPU, and do not infer physical CPU/energy improvement from guest clocks.

reviewed_boundary_observations: Canonical authorization, signatures, encryption, replay and reply matching remain in the adapter/MVM boundary, independently reviewed elsewhere; this review checked the live caller configuration and lifecycle rather than re-approving that implementation.
Expected public fixtures are independently regenerated for verification and are not inserted into the receiver cache.
The relay forwards bounded opaque canonical envelopes and checks provisioned public outer route metadata; it does not decrypt.
Session success requires matching directional counters, byte-exact stopped-store readback and clean worker completion. The two-guest session adds a keyless read-only verifier reboot.

Final guest cleanup drains public console records before mount/unmount printk, attempts data synchronization/unmount after workload failure, and prevents clean completion if final console draining fails.
Fresh private directories/files, bounded boot inputs and console capture, owned worker reaping, checked disk synchronization, persistent result journaling and fail-closed completion were examined.
security_and_claim_limits: The trusted launcher generates and provisions signing and encryption keys. Opaque relay forwarding does not prove confidentiality against a compromised host or launcher.
This is an experimental local actual-MVM/vsock integration, not a deployed production mailbox, FIPS validation, CUI authorization or WAN qualification.
The keyless verifier reboot proves historical persisted bytes. It does not prove new-epoch authenticated network resume or durable mailbox delivery.
The registered pilot has one trial per cell. It cannot establish stable latency distributions or statistical performance superiority.
Guest process CPU accounting is not qualified as physical energy or complete endpoint cost. Existing receipts require the explicit accounting-domain and receive-work limitations.
The pinned native kernel baseline allows its documented two known OtherException exits; this is not an unrestricted exception acceptance rule or a register-level qualification.
